title: Topological dimension at the zero section of a polynomial algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $B$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $r\geq0$, and $C=B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ let $\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak q C+(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$, the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ under evaluation $C\to B$ at zero. Then, for affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and topological dimension at a point [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], both dimensions in the following formula are finite nonnegative integers and $$\dim_{\mathfrak Q}\operatorname{Spec}C=\dim_{\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Spec}B+r.$$ No reducedness, equidimensionality or perfectness hypothesis is imposed. For $B=0$ there is no prime $\mathfrak q$, and the assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field), dimension at a point as the maximum dimension of components through it; Tag 00P0 (lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring), dimension of each finite type domain equals transcendence degree. Applied to the components of polynomial affine space over Spec B.

proof.text: Choose finite algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ for $B$. Together with $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ they generate $C$ over $k$, so $C$ is finite type by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Evaluation at zero followed by $B\to B/\mathfrak q$ is surjective and has kernel $\mathfrak Q$: a polynomial $f$ lies in that kernel exactly when its constant coefficient $f(0)$ lies in $\mathfrak q$, and since $f-f(0)\in(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ this holds exactly when $f\in\mathfrak qC+(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$; conversely $\mathfrak qC+(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ maps into $\mathfrak q$. In particular $\mathfrak Q\cap B=\mathfrak q$. Thus $C/\mathfrak Q\cong B/\mathfrak q$ is a nonzero domain, and $\mathfrak Q$ is prime. This also verifies that the point in the statement exists.

source.place: Tag 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field), component-maximum formula; polynomial component calculation using the coefficient description of polynomials and Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Polynomial.lean:120-121

proof.text: For every ideal $\mathfrak a\subset B$, coefficient reduction gives $C/\mathfrak aC\cong(B/\mathfrak a)[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$: its kernel consists exactly of polynomials all of whose coefficients lie in $\mathfrak a$, each a sum of coefficient multiples of monomials. If $\mathfrak a$ is prime, this quotient is a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain], so $\mathfrak aC$ is prime and contracts to $\mathfrak a$. If $P$ is a minimal prime of $C$, choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak a\subset P\cap B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]. Then $\mathfrak aC\subset P$ is prime, so $P=\mathfrak aC$. Conversely, if $\mathfrak a$ is minimal and a prime $P\subset\mathfrak aC$, contraction gives $P\cap B=\mathfrak a$ and hence $\mathfrak aC\subset P$, proving minimality. Finally $\mathfrak aC\subset\mathfrak Q$ if and only if $\mathfrak a\subset\mathfrak q$, by contraction and extension. These operations are inverse bijections on the indicated minimal primes.

source.place: Tag 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field), component-maximum formula; polynomial component calculation using the coefficient description of polynomials and Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Polynomial.lean:120-121

proof.text: For each minimal prime $\mathfrak a\subset\mathfrak q$, the images of the chosen $b_j$ generate $B/\mathfrak a$ over $k$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $B/\mathfrak a$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] with the $r$ variables to the coefficient-reduction isomorphism of step 2, obtaining $$\dim(C/\mathfrak aC)=\dim(B/\mathfrak a)+r.$$ A ring isomorphism gives inverse inclusion-preserving maps on prime ideals, so preserves these dimensions directly from their definition [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Tag 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field), component-maximum formula; polynomial component calculation using the coefficient description of polynomials and Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Polynomial.lean:120-121

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components] first to $(B,\mathfrak q)$ and then to $(C,\mathfrak Q)$; both are finite type over the same field by step 1. Its minimal-prime formulation gives a finite nonempty list $\mathfrak a_1,\ldots,\mathfrak a_t$ below $\mathfrak q$, and by step 2 the corresponding list below $\mathfrak Q$ is $\mathfrak a_iC$. Thus step 3 gives $$\dim_{\mathfrak Q}\operatorname{Spec}C=\max_i(\dim(B/\mathfrak a_i)+r)=\max_i\dim(B/\mathfrak a_i)+r=\dim_{\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Spec}B+r.$$ The middle equality holds because adding $r$ preserves order and a finite nonempty maximum is attained. The same cited theorem asserts that each dimension at a point is a finite nonnegative integer. For $r=0$ the calculation is unchanged; for $B=0$ there is no prime and nothing to prove.
